supply_voltage.source: Pololu Balboa 32U4 Balancing Robot User's Guide §3.6: six AA cells; 1.2 V nominal per NiMH cell

supply_voltage_max.source: derived: 6 cells x approximately 1.4 V open-circuit per fully charged NiMH cell (Energizer NiMH Handbook)

no_change_justified.electrical.motor_left: the MP motor at the 8.4 V maximum supply against this driver. Current: its 0.94 A stall current is 0.52 of the 1.8 A recommended peak current and 0.49 of the 1.9 A minimum overcurrent trip (TA = 25 C). Voltage: 8.4 V is 0.78 of the board's 10.8 V. Basis: the maker's recommended operating conditions. The datasheet's recommended operating table gives no separate continuous rating. Nothing here changes.

current_limit.source: TI DRV8838 datasheet SLVSBA4F §6.3 Recommended Operating Conditions: IOUT motor peak current, max 1.8 A

overcurrent_trip_min.source: TI DRV8838 datasheet SLVSBA4F §6.5 Electrical Characteristics, TA = 25 C: IOCP overcurrent trip, min 1.9 A

rated_voltage.source: the stricter of two: Pololu Balboa 32U4 Balancing Robot User's Guide §3.6, the board's VIN is limited to 10.8 V by the DRV8838; the chip's own VM maximum is 11 V (TI DRV8838 datasheet SLVSBA4F §6.3)

continuous_current_max.source: rule of thumb: Pololu's general recommendation of 25% or less of the stall current for brushed DC motors (Pololu item #2365, 50:1 Micro Metal Gearmotor MP 6V, product page and Micro Metal Gearmotor datasheet rev 6.2, read 16.10.2026), applied to the stall current at the maximum supply

stall_current.source: Pololu item #2365, 50:1 Micro Metal Gearmotor MP 6V, product page and Micro Metal Gearmotor datasheet rev 6.2, read 16.10.2026: stall current 0.67 A at 6 V, extrapolated (theoretical)

stall_current_at_supply_max.source: derived: 0.67 A x 8.4 V / 6 V = 0.94 A; stall current scales with the applied voltage: derived from Microchip AN905 p. 2 (current linear with torque) and p. 6 (back-EMF proportional to speed); series resistances of the driver, wiring and battery would only lower it

stall_duration_max.source: the design's limit, handed to the firmware role: a stall is ended by cutting the drive after 1 s; Pololu warns that stalls can cause thermal damage to the windings and brushes 'potentially on the order of seconds' (Pololu item #2365, 50:1 Micro Metal Gearmotor MP 6V, product page and Micro Metal Gearmotor datasheet rev 6.2, read 16.10.2026)

supply_voltage_max_applied.source: the given battery's maximum; the 6 V motor runs above its rated voltage, which Pololu notes could start affecting the motor's life (Pololu item #2365, 50:1 Micro Metal Gearmotor MP 6V, product page and Micro Metal Gearmotor datasheet rev 6.2, read 16.10.2026)

stall_torque.source: derived: 0.54 kg·cm extrapolated stall torque (Pololu item #2365, 50:1 Micro Metal Gearmotor MP 6V, product page and Micro Metal Gearmotor datasheet rev 6.2, read 16.10.2026) x 9.80665 N/kg x 0.01 m/cm x 8.4 V / 6 V; stall torque scales with stall current, and stall current scales with the applied voltage: derived from Microchip AN905 p. 2 (current linear with torque) and p. 6 (back-EMF proportional to speed)

allowable_stress.source: BASF Forward AM, 3D Printing Materials & Solutions, Spring 2023, Mechanical Properties Comparison table: Ultrafuse PLA ISO 527 tensile strength ZX, 21.2 MPa, typical value, unverified until tested; the root stress crosses the layers

bending_stress.source: derived: 6 x 7.41 N x 0.008 m / (0.006 m x (0.003 m)^2); Euler-Bernoulli cantilever, sigma = 6 F L / (b h^2) (Roylance, MIT 3.11, Stresses in Beams); a short tab, so shear and the root fillet's stress concentration are not included

factor_of_safety.source: the design's stated factor on ultimate: no published factor covers printed plastic, so it takes 2.0, the analysis-only FOSU of ECSS-E-ST-32-10C Rev.2 Corr.1 Table 4-3 for metallic, FRP and sandwich parts of satellites and launch vehicles, as a reference from a stricter class, not as physics. length.source: the design's choice; BASF Ultrafuse PLA, FDM; the tab is printed with its 8 mm length along the build (Z) axis, so the root bending stress crosses the layers; printed upright on its 6 mm face, no overhang, 0.5 mm chamfer on the bed edges; 0.2 mm layers, 100% infill, 4 perimeters

load_force.source: derived: stall-torque reaction as a couple, F = T / s = 0.0741 N·m / 0.01 m per tab

spacing.source: the design's choice: the two tabs' centre distance
